observances: Speak the names of the line at the evening meal.
Ask the elders before any great choice.
Keep the hearth fed.
Say a short prayer before every meal.

prayers: Fingihe, light of the first morning, hold back the Shadow Under from this house tonight.
I light the gas lamp against the Shadow Under, and ask Fingihe to stand beside it.
Two powers pull the world; Fingihe, be the stronger in my hands.
Fingihe, in the long war, count me a soldier, not a prize.
Make me gentle to the beast and the beggar, Fingihe, even when they are not gentle to me.
Fingihe, let my hands be a bowl for the hungry and a roof for the cold.

liturgy.name: The Rite of Open Hands
steps: The chapel doors are opened and the sick and hungry are led in before the faithful.
The abbot of mercy washes the hands of the first guest.
A common pot is served to all, beggar and elder alike.
The wounded are tended in a side room while a verse is read.
The printed psalter is read, a little, by the gas lamp.
The abbot of mercy asks aloud who is without a bed tonight and finds one.
The faithful leave in pairs and carry what is left to the doors of the sick.

scripture.title: The Songs of the First Light
excerpts: Law: In every choice, ask which power it feeds.
Parable of the Bowl: A man gave his last bowl to a stranger and found it full each morning.
Verse: Feed the one before you; the one behind you will be fed by another.
Verse: The wound you ease is the wound you carry.
Law: A guest is fed before they are asked their name.
Verse: Two hands made the world: one lit it, one was jealous.
Verse: Mercy is not weakness, but a harder kind of strength.
Law: You shall not lie to the light, nor flatter the dark.
Verse: the Shadow Under does not hate you. It only waits.

saints.name: Saint Wikinima the Blood-Witness
saints.legend: Wikinima sang the old hymn until the end, and the singing was taken up by those who watched. Canonised in year 150.

saints.name: Muriha the Lamp-bearer
saints.legend: Muriha judged a feud between brothers and left both of them in tears of shame.

heresies.name: Waweite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the true line of teaching was broken by the abbot of mercy of the mother faith.

heresies.name: The Salt Brothers
heresies.claim: Holds that flesh may be eaten without sin.

heresies.name: The Strict Mercy
heresies.claim: Holds that mercy to the wicked is cruelty to the good.

heresies.name: The Sharp-Handed
heresies.claim: Holds that the sick are punished and should not be healed.

lore.afterlife: After death the soul stands on a narrow bridge; what it carried decides which way it leans.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Common Pot
holyDays.rite: All households bring one dish to a shared table in the square.

holyDays.name: The Hospice Days
holyDays.rite: The faithful tend the sick in the chapel for three days without pay.

holyDays.name: Day of Gentle Hands
holyDays.rite: No animal is slaughtered; the faithful eat only what the earth gives.

holyDays.name: The Healing Walk
holyDays.rite: The abbot of mercy walks the streets and blesses every invalid door.

holyDays.name: Night of the Lamps for the Lost
holyDays.rite: A gas lamp is set at the door for each missing soul.

blessings: May you be healed as you heal.
May you be fed as you feed.
May the road be kind to your feet.
sins: striking a child or an animal
breaking a vow sworn at the chapel
defiling the chapel with a brawl

clergy.greetStranger: Your name can wait. Warm yourself first.
clergy.title: Abbot of Mercy

observances: Eat no flesh on holy days.
Give away a tenth of what you have.
Forgive one wrong each month.
Give a tithe to the chapel each season.

prayers: We are the leaves, Lonesopo is the root; let the root drink well.
Let the dead be fed and the living honoured, Lonesopo, in that order.
Blood of Lonesopo, blood in me; let me not shame the name.
I set out loaf and the gas lamp for those who walked here before.
Lonesopo, send me to the door that has not heard your name.
Give me words for the stranger, Lonesopo, and ears for the stranger’s answer.

liturgy.name: The Open Door Hour
steps: The steam whistle sounds and the doors of the chapel are propped wide.
A new face is sought and welcomed by name before anything else.
The apostolic overseer tells the story of Lonesopo in plain words.
The congregation sings the long hymn, loud enough for the street.
Testimony: any may stand and say what Lonesopo has done for them.
The faithful are paired with those who are new.
The apostolic overseer names the road for the next sending, and who goes.
Everyone leaves carrying a copy of the first verse to give away.

scripture.title: The Songs of Seven Winters
excerpts: Law: Speak of the dead as you speak to the living, and listen as well.
Parable of the Shut Gate: A town barred its walls and the faith went round them like water.
Verse: A house without a grave has not been lived in.
Parable of the Sower: A man threw seed on stone and soil alike, and was told he was right.
Verse: The stranger is a guest of Lonesopo before they are a guest of yours.
Verse: Lonesopo wore the first crown so you might not have to.
Verse: A lamp that is only shown to the house is a poor lamp.
Law: The eldest speaks first and the youngest keeps the lamp.
Law: Answer a question once with the truth, and a second time with patience.

saints.name: Nefamema the Unbroken
saints.legend: Nefamema judged a feud between brothers and left both of them in tears of shame.

saints.name: Noga the Unbroken
saints.legend: Noga gave away the whole of a rich inheritance and died with only a bowl.

saints.name: Mesa the Unbroken
saints.legend: Mesa walked into a burning chapel and returned with the printed psalter and no scorch.

heresies.name: Mebaite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the true line of teaching was broken by the apostolic overseer of the mother faith.

heresies.name: The Closed Door
heresies.claim: Holds that the faith need not be spread, only lived.

heresies.name: The Silent Flock
heresies.claim: Holds that conversion by song is no conversion at all.

heresies.name: The Word Kept
heresies.claim: Holds that Lonesopo speaks differently to each people and none should be taught another’s word.

lore.afterlife: A good ancestor dwells in the hearth and is fed; a forgotten one goes cold.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Open Door
holyDays.rite: Every house sets a place at table for a stranger.

holyDays.name: Day of Testimony
holyDays.rite: Any may stand in the square and tell what Lonesopo has done.

holyDays.name: The Welcoming
holyDays.rite: New converts are named before the town and given the first loaf.

blessings: May every door open to your voice.
May you find a hundred listeners.
May the work of your hands outlast you.
sins: refusing to give the first verse
turning a seeker from the door
breaking a vow sworn at the chapel

clergy.greetFaithful: Well met, {name}. The harvest is wide.
clergy.greetStranger: Stranger, come in; there is a place and a word for you.
clergy.title: Apostolic Overseer

observances: Welcome a stranger to your table once a week.
Support a mission each season.
Keep a spare printed psalter for the curious.
Say a short prayer before every meal.

prayers: All roads end in you, Shubrash; lead my feet and the feet of Dimtamkid.
One maker, one judge: Shubrash, weigh me gently and do not look away.
Shubrash, light the gas lamp in me that I may see my own faults first.
Shubrash, one and only, keep this house under your single eye.
Grant that I be born again to the rank I earn by doing this one well.
Let each keep the post Shubrash set, the hand to the plough and the mind to the book.

liturgy.name: The Ordered Hours
steps: The faithful enter by the door of their station, the high first and the low last.
The high brahmin lights the gas lamp and names the duty of each rank aloud.
Each rank answers with its own line of the creed.
The printed psalter is read from the page of the day.
Each house brings its tithe in the goods of its trade.
The high brahmin blesses the tithe, and the lowest rank is fed first, as the rule requires.
The vows of station are renewed together.
The ranks leave in reverse, and no one speaks across a boundary until the door is passed.

scripture.title: The Law of the Open Hand
excerpts: Law: Marry within your station; the line is the first obligation.
Law: The seventh day is Shubrash’s; let the ox and the servant rest with you.
Verse: The humblest duty done well outweighs the highest done ill.
Verse: Every hair on your head is counted, and not one wasted.
Verse: A rank is not a cage but a bridge for the one who walks it with grace.
Law: The high shall not strike the low; the low shall not speak first to the high.
Parable of the Lamp: A man hid his gas lamp under a bowl, and walked into a well.
Law: You shall bear no second name before Shubrash, neither in jest nor in need.
Parable of the Potter’s Son: He turned a scribe and spoiled both trades.

saints.name: Saint Chachiñuha the Compassionate
saints.legend: Chachiñuha gave a cloak to a beggar who was later found to be Shubrash in disguise. Canonised in year 110.

saints.name: Saint Rehi the Shieldbearer
saints.legend: Rehi held the ford at Dide alone for a night and a day, and the river ran red around them. Canonised in year 70.

saints.name: Saint Kha the Blood-Witness
saints.legend: Kha walked unarmed to the enemy camp and was killed; the army broke camp the next morning. Canonised in year 10.

heresies.name: Sinnayite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the holy days were moved and the old calendar is the right one.

heresies.name: The Open Station
heresies.claim: Holds that the high brahmin are only men and may be wrong about stations.

heresies.name: The Crossed Hands
heresies.claim: Holds that marriage across ranks is blessed by Shubrash.

heresies.name: The Levellers of the Quarter
heresies.claim: Holds that the tithe of the low is worth more than the high’s.

lore.afterlife: The faithful wake in the house of Shubrash, where there is no hunger and every door stands open.

holyDays.name: Day of Stations
holyDays.rite: Each rank renews its vows in order before the high brahmin.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Four Tools
holyDays.rite: Plough, pen, sword and scales are blessed on the chapel steps.

holyDays.name: The Walk of the Gate
holyDays.rite: All ranks walk the boundary of the quarter and mend what is broken.

holyDays.name: The Weighing of Tithes
holyDays.rite: Houses bring the year’s goods and the lowest rank is fed first.

holyDays.name: Night of the Returning
holyDays.rite: The faithful recite the names of past lives, one rank at a time.

blessings: May your house be known for its craft.
May the rank bless you as you bless it.
May your table never be bare.
sins: taking up a trade not your own
refusing the tithe of your house
breaking a vow sworn at the chapel

clergy.greetFaithful: Hail, {name}. Keep your station and be at peace.
clergy.greetStranger: Traveller, state your house and rank, and I will know how to greet you.
clergy.title: High Brahmin

observances: Renew station vows each new year.
Bring the tithe of your trade.

people.look: A compact and muscular Crimson-Shell Behemoth-Brood figure with slate-grey eyes, glossy iridescent mandibles and compound facets, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Ñalana
people.title: Sapa Inca of ÑukaTawantin
people.look: A statuesque Black-Fur Plague-Skulk figure with storm-grey eyes, twitching whiskers, notched ears, and keen ruby eyes, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Grupru
people.title: Imperator of Cruvrenre
people.look: A graceful Bone-Purple Leviathan-Brood figure with pale ice-blue eyes, chitinous cranial crest and twitching antennae, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Yopo
people.title: Oba of Wewọ
people.look: A broad-shouldered Crimson-Shell Behemoth-Brood figure with dark obsidian eyes, glossy iridescent mandibles and compound facets, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Gravlumri
people.title: Imperator of Flipri
people.look: A tall and gaunt Bone-Purple Leviathan-Brood figure with slate-grey eyes, chitinous cranial crest and twitching antennae, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Hañukala
people.title: Sapa Inca of Piñarasuyu
people.look: A statuesque Brindle Steppe-Herd figure with bright gold eyes, sleek brindled fur and ascarred snout, and calloused hands stained with ink and oil. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

events.text: NATURE BLESSING: Sylvanor the Forest Horn awakens the ancient canopies of Reda! Verdant thickets ensnare enemies and provide abundant woodland forage (+16 stability, +10% army power).
Unrest of the year: sectarian clashes in Frentum (Nojajokapu).

Llagra of Cruvrenre comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Dago III of Sisukago secures the line, with Sihuka grown to take the crown.
Pichini of Mibo comes to the throne bent on glory.
Blikhra of Flipri comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Yoro conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Iron Plains) using assault (score 18 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Wugeda survived descent to Layer 2 (Forest of Whispers), enduring 13 strain damage: Nausea, severe headaches, and limb numbness upon ascent. Whistle tier: blue.
Jurists of Vrelrona codify the law at Vrelrona; disputes are settled by writ, not sword.
Furs and amber from Tlusk reach the great fair at Tlograd.
The Hollow School of Vrelrona takes shape in Vrelrona: painters who break with the old canons.
Whispers in the fields of Duribọba: a movement of free tenants gathers the company hands against company towns.
A brown smog settles over Sonemayu in Tenipa; children cough in the mill streets and the well-to-do flee to the hills.
The tiny Rift-Dominion of Shretripur seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Hepopo.
Daci squeezes the shaft-tolls of Flicrona; the miners of Flicrona mutter beneath the stone.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Kvugorod bars the shaft to Vliclu, and the tithe-collectors of Lokhkür are turned back at the lamps of Kvugorod.
FLOOD: The Tariha bursts its banks in late spring; the low quarters of Hemula are under water and the harvest of Hilite rots in the fields.
The Sanitary Board of ÑukaTawantin lays sewers and lime-washes Dide; the Brown Vapours loses its grip.
Regency established: with young monarch Bamfiza at age 7, Lord Regent Pasknash assumes the seal of state for Dakhgird.
Canoe Launching: People of Vohi wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Womunemotu.
Yam Feast: Granaries of Fulomu are opened at Fulomu; the whole town eats until dusk.
Envoys from Chonini and Guka exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Lokhkür and Qödgibböz exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
A victor's peace is forged: after 3 years of campaign in the Guka–Kil-hycame War, Guka prevail, annexing contested borderlands.
Humbled, Free Trading Cities of Kil-hycame bends the knee and becomes a vassal of Guka, paying yearly tribute.
Wawe of Guka wins the glory sought in the Guka–Kil-hycame War.
ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Following decisive defeat in war, Guka imposes constitutional terms upon Kil-hycame! The former rulers are ousted, and the Grand Marshalate of Kil-hycame is inaugurated.
Nizlömkal of Chöshjum takes up the cause of wealth.
Dynastic extinction strikes Chöshjum: Dükkingula dies heirless (poison). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Zokhjir claims the vacant crown.
Llucli of Cruvrenre takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
The death of Llagra Vriqlivlavle (battle wounds) leaves Cruvrenre without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Lleqlius seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Kahowute take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Vohi, they hoist republican banners beneath Remule to establish the Confederation of Kahowute.
Remule is acclaimed ruler of Confederation of Kahowute.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Principality of Vohi dispatches punitive legions to subdue Confederation of Kahowute. The bitter Vohi Succession War is underway.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Wemapee take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Hilite, they hoist republican banners beneath Mugi to establish the Republic of Wemapee.
Mugi is acclaimed ruler of Republic of Wemapee.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Grand Marshalate of Hilite marches swiftly upon Republic of Wemapee. The drums of the War of Hilite echo across the provinces.
Siynaylaba (Grand Champion) sets an unprecedented record in the sprint and javelin throwing trials in Famlam.
Shulbiz (Archmage) weaves a protective arcane ward over the city walls in Halshij.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Sonamọba! Nayransaq seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Artificer Directorate of Sonamọba!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Fulomu as a mass uprising topples the throne of Free Commonwealth of Fulomu! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Uge proclaims the sovereign People's Republic of Fulomu!
QUEST COMPLETED: Quest for the Lost War Standard of Biqnoszoq! Khojköma raises the standard over the camp and the clans cheer, giving the sacred relic Shattered Tiara of Linoludotere!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Cigawudi pave the Giwatach-Nonumoho Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Giwatach and Nonumoho (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Vohi pave the Womunemotu-Fireharoa Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Womunemotu and Fireharoa (+trade, +stability).
The Sedagidan–Noginebu Railway of Sonamọba reaches Lorawe: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
RUINOUS GIFT: Tzannik the Architect of Fate mutates the weave of fate in Kegonani! Arcane mutations grant uncanny clairvoyance and secret gold, at the cost of civil panic (+30 gold, -6 stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Khorvath the Blood Lord floods the warriors of Nojajokapu with bloodthirsty slaughter! Mortal legions butcher foes with demonic savagery (+25% army power, -8 stability).
Clockwork icons appear on Giwatach lampposts: the Society of the Last Cog preaches that flesh must be replaced by brass.
The Smoke Prophets gathers in the boiler vaults beneath Ile-wolu, worshipping a great engine that, they swear, dreams.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Panuwa (Chonini).

Nayransaq of Sonamọba comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
Cafa of Cigawudi lets go of the aim for glory.
Uge of Fulomu comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Uge of Fulomu fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.
Ure conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Iron Plains) using assault (score 33 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Je'jo survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 6 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
Furs and amber from Tlusk reach the great fair at Tlograd.
Nations of Mihopah gather at Mawokuni for a great council and dances that last through the night.
Nocho lifts its measures against the Womatuvimiro. Few believe it will last, but the burnings stop.
Soldiers scatter a league of the landless in Vrelrona; Vrelrona keeps company towns by force.
Flipri squeezes the shaft-tolls of Ntomir; the miners of Kvugorod mutter beneath the stone.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Sa'lektun close the air-lanes above Tefahu, starving Vohi of the high trade.
SEA EMBARGO: Sisukago seals the deep channels, and no hull leaves the port of Veftrolv for Vemhog.
Rains swell the Tariha until it takes the bridges of Hemula; whole villages float away downstream.
Regency established: with young monarch Uge at age 15, Lord Regent Ure assumes the seal of state for Fulomu.
Regency established: with young monarch Terula at age 3, Lord Regent Cyga assumes the seal of state for Kil-hycame.
Bloodline awakened: Mine of Mona manifests the hereditary Red Miasma curse across Chonini.
Geothermal eruption: superheated magma overflows the crucibles of Kil-hycame; artisan holds suffer heavy damage.
The Guka–Kil-hycame War is known as the Liberation among the Yoheche, and as the Betrayal among the Nusi.
Hepopo's invasion through the Hollow Door into Siny was repulsed at Kvakvi.
Night of Pomegranates: The longest night in Vemhog is spent by firelight in Veftpush, with stories and gifts.
Water Festival: People of Tenipa wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Mite.
Day of Rain Offerings: People of Ke'ka wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Chete.
After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Wemapee give way! Vanguard forces of Hilite storm the royal seat of Wemapee, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
Festival of the Ancestors: Families in Sonamọba set out lamps and food for their dead at Rabumedo.
Envoys from Chonini and Nachonaki exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.

Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: People's Republic of Fulomu launches a determined invasion into Free Commonwealth of Tuchawamipa, igniting the Conquest of Tuchawamipa. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Suchino rally to Tuchawamipa's side.
Glullu II of Vrelrona turns from the old cause toward vengeance.
The bells of Vrelrona toll for the passing of Glullu Pius Pruvlius (battle wounds). The youth Glullu ascends the throne under a regency council.
Defying the crown of Vemhog, the garrison and civic guilds of Khonnabad mutiny! The sovereign Cybernetic Union of Vemkoz is declared with Kufgigda at its helm.
Kufgigda is acclaimed ruler of Cybernetic Union of Vemkoz.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Syndicate of Vemhog dispatches punitive legions to subdue Cybernetic Union of Vemkoz. The bitter Vemkoz Succession War is underway.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Wakawoma storm the government palace in Chonini! The faction seizes control, establishing the Divine Realm of Chonini.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Gohonoke storm the government palace in Yunuwagi! The faction seizes control, establishing the Polytechnic League of Yunuwagi.

STATE ATHEISM PROCLAIMED: The revolutionary leadership in Yunuwagi enacts Radical Secularization! State religion is abolished, temple estates and monastery vaults are confiscated for the people (+65 gold), and ancient dogma is suppressed.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Assassins from Vrelrona strike in the dead of night, slaying Gulife in the court of Daci!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Vrelrona are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Daci!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Vohi divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Dölzüj!

ARCANE MELTDOWN: Unstable alchemy and runaway leyline containment experiments detonate violently near Arcane Proving Grounds of Cell 5099! Magical shockwaves scorch the earth into irradiated ash, collapsing towers and displacing hundreds.
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Wugeda embarks upon the Saving the Terraces of Ngadayu Before the Rains! Wugeda hears that the terrace walls above Ngadayu are cracking just before the planting season.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Polego pave the Gilọ-Sowegodan Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Gilọ and Sowegodan (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Fulomu pave the Mufufofe-Pere Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Mufufofe and Pere (+trade, +stability).
The Chakiñi–Lukiru Railway of Piñarasuyu reaches Chamarca: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
The Ganiwowa–Panuwa Railway opens: the first railway of Chonini runs from Ganiwowa to Panuwa, with stations in both towns.

DIVINE PROXY WAR: The war between Vemhog and Vemkoz escalates into a celestial proxy duel! Pestilax the Rot-Father rallies the hosts of Vemhog, while Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer unleashes sacred omens to shield Vemkoz.
RUINOUS GIFT: Luxuria the Gilded Prince intoxicates the high courts of Tuchawamipa with exquisite hedonism! Opulence surges alongside reckless decadence (+40 gold, -10 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Ignis the Hearth Caldera stokes the caldera hearths of Wemapee! Master smiths forge shimmering obsidian weaponry bathed in magma (+16% army power, +15 gold).
Masked engineer Yopo sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Pere; workers whisper the name in every pub.
Crowds in Wewekuta hang on the words of Uge, who calls for an eight-hour day as holy writ.
Masked engineer Nu'a sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Yuko'iha; workers whisper the name in every pub.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Sisukago.

Bunnimduha of Tenipa lets go of the aim for the spread of the faith.
Wakawoma of Chonini comes to the throne bent on knowledge.
Gohonoke of Yunuwagi comes to the throne bent on the safety of the nation.
Blikhra of Flipri fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.
Glullu II of Vrelrona lets the old grudge rest as the foe is no more.
House Zhakhlod of Vemkoz and House Rihkmigzab of Dakhgird were joined in royal marriage.
Nzubsa conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Iron Plains) using tactic (score 29 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Tuha survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 9 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
The Hollow School of Vrelrona finds patrons in Clevru.
Borne on the winds, Ix-cha now drifts above the lands of Vohi.
Daci squeezes the shaft-tolls of Flicrona; the miners of Flicrona mutter beneath the stone.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Ke'ka close the air-lanes above Ngarateke, starving Vohi of the high trade.
Dudasekota raises its port toll at Dakhgird; the harbour-masters of Dakhgird protest.
HURRICANE: A great storm comes out of the warm sea in high summer; Tiwe loses its roofs and its fleet, and the coast of Tenipa is drowned in surge.
A sickness the people call the Tiwe Gripe breaks out in Tiwe; the bells of Tenipa toll for its first dead.
A mountainside gives way above Fireharoa; houses, a road and a mill are buried in a single roar of mud and stone.
Where the Tariha left its silt, the fields of Hemula now yield double; Hilite remembers the flood with mixed feelings.
Uge of Fulomu attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Regency established: with young monarch Glullu at age 4, Lord Regent Grublecli assumes the seal of state for Vrelrona.
Bloodline awakened: Glifra of Pruglu manifests the hereditary Seer Lunacy curse across Frentum.
After 39 months, the Brown Vapours is gone; Litoholeti counts the empty houses.
Feast of New Light: People of Vemkoz wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Khonnabad.
Feast of Breaking the Fast: Bonfires on the hills of Ramsufsuffan greet the high sun above Zandim.
Feast of the Vine: Granaries of Vrelrona are opened at Vrelrona; the whole town eats until dusk.
The sun sets upon Republic of Wemapee. Bereft of armies and abandoned by vassals, the nation collapses into history; Mugi Nokenemeni escapes into the wilderness.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of Hilite after 1 year. With frontiers redrawn, Hilite dictate terms to the vanquished.
Envoys from Litoholeti and Ramsufsuffan exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Mine of Chonini takes up the cause of a lasting legacy.
In Chonini, Wakawoma the Shrewd Chakoge departs this life, succumbing to old age. The child Mine (age 3) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Te Vufila take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Vohi, they hoist republican banners beneath Wawukata to establish the Democratic Union of Tafelenui.
Wawukata is acclaimed ruler of Democratic Union of Tafelenui.

Outraged by treason, the crown of Principality of Vohi mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Democratic Union of Tafelenui. The Tafelenui Succession War begins in fire and iron.
A bloody conspiracy in the capital: General Framlia marches veterans into the council hall, deposing Glifra and proclaiming military rule over Frentum.
Glifra III of Frentum turns from the old cause toward the safety of the nation.
In the royal halls of Frentum, Glifra II the Frail Pruglu breathes their last, succumbing to the coup. Glifra ascends the ancestral throne amid solemn acclamation.
Framlia of Frentum turns from the old cause toward glory.
Framlia takes the throne of Frentum.
Wi'kasa (Grand Champion) sweeps all contenders in the Grand Tourney to ecstatic cheers from thousands in Sa'lektun.
Rosa (Master Artisan) unveils a breathtaking marble colossus in the central plaza in Dipazhou.
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Nomzekjima strike at midnight in Chöshjum! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the High Realm of Chöshjum!
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Mijicho storm the government palace in Suchino! The faction seizes control, establishing the Protectorate of Suchino.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Vrelrona storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Gracra proclaims the foundation of the Free Union of Vrelrona!

STATE ATHEISM PROCLAIMED: The revolutionary leadership in Vrelrona enacts Radical Secularization! State religion is abolished, temple estates and monastery vaults are confiscated for the people (+65 gold), and ancient dogma is suppressed.

NATURE BLESSING: Undina of the Silver Basin purifies the sacred rivers of Frentum! Abundant fish and unhindered river trade enrich the townships (+30 gold, +12 stability).

The Smoke Prophets gathers in the boiler vaults beneath Sisukago, worshipping a great engine that, they swear, dreams.
Pokumacha, an aeronaut outlaw, raids the payroll zeppelins of Hilite and drops the coin over the slums of Wemapee.
Ute, a soot-stained visionary, preaches in the Fulomu smokestacks that the age of iron will end in fire and renewal.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Debulag (Chogbulag); tax riots in Gorithani (Dudasekota); tax riots in Sa'lektun.
A notorious bandit encampment, Gorithani Outlaw Lair, arose outside Gorithani.

Ke'laba of Sa'lektun attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Terula of Kil-hycame attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Glullu of Vrelrona attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
The Bipifọ Campaign is known as the Aggression among the Nizdvig, and as the Vindication among the Noku.
Feast of the Return Voyage: Boats of Hilite are blessed and raced off Hemula; sailors are toasted ashore.
The White Cough burns itself out at last; survivors in Vohi bury the dead and open the shutters.
Following fierce fighting along the fortifications, Yuko'iha surrenders to Sonamọba; its magistrates swear fealty as Nojajokapu's banner is hauled down.
Festival of the Ancestors: Families in Nurore set out lamps and food for their dead at Gusefe.
Envoys from Qasr Fab and Litoholeti exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Fulomu and Chusuyu exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Lokhkür and Qödgibböz exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Ambition stirs in the courts of Military Junta of Vrelrona, which openly claims dominion over Free City of Blia. The nation braces as the Hundred Days War of Blia erupts.
Vakiveme of Hepopo turns from the old cause toward the spread of the faith.
In Hepopo, Zekchaza the Unready Nonbukh departs this life, succumbing to a fall from a horse. The child Vakiveme (age 7) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.
Tojana of Mibo comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Solemn rites echo through Mibo following the death of Pichini the Lame Wochomu (fever). Tojana is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Wuladi rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Vohi, they establish the Commune of Hifiwesy with Fedeta leading the commune.
Fedeta is acclaimed ruler of Commune of Hifiwesy.
Outraged by treason, the crown of Cybernetic Union of Vohi mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Commune of Hifiwesy. The Great Vohi War begins in fire and iron.

MERCANTILE SECESSION: Wealthy patricians and merchant cartels in Frentum rebel against royal tariffs! Declaring commercial independence from Nojajokapu, Frevria establishes the Trade Federation of Frentum.
Frevria is acclaimed ruler of Trade Federation of Frentum.

Outraged by treason, the crown of Merchant League of Nojajokapu mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Trade Federation of Frentum. The Conquest of Frentum begins in fire and iron.
Wi'kasa (Grand Champion) bestows glorious sporting renown upon the host realm in the international games in Sa'lektun.
Siynaylaba (Grand Champion) defeats a formidable foreign dragoon in single combat before the royal court in Famlam.
Derepome (Master Artificer) engineers a revolutionary watermill mechanism that doubles grain milling yields in Tosesemolowe.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Ziyzid storm the government palace in Qasr Fab! The faction seizes control, establishing the Protectorate of Qasr Fab.
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Mimapa strike at midnight in Hilite! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Protectorate of Hilite!
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Grufla storm the government palace in Frentum! The faction seizes control, establishing the Merchant League of Frentum.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Daci pave the Cigari-Titu Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Cigari and Titu (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Babfazh pave the Babfazh-Miheton Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Babfazh and Miheton (+trade, +stability).
The Te Vufila–Hilite Railway opens: the first railway of Tafelenui runs from Te Vufila to Hilite, with stations in both towns.
PATRON MIRACLE: Omnipotis the Sovereign Architect manifests the Sovereign Mandate in Chöshjum! Incorruptible celestial magistrates codify sacred law, crushing unrest (+20 stability, +15 gold).
RUINOUS GIFT: Tzannik the Architect of Fate mutates the weave of fate in Kegonani! Arcane mutations grant uncanny clairvoyance and secret gold, at the cost of civil panic (+30 gold, -6 stability).
ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Blia! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Zephyros the Sky-Sovereign hurls deafening thunderbolts across the frontiers of Nusachu, scattering hostile vanguards with righteous gales (+15% army power).
ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Shubbog the Brood Mother spawns thousands of chittering dark young in the sacred groves of Hifiwesy, swarming forward under black skies (+20% army power, -6 stability).

A child of two peoples, Runmlidy Fizzabapur Yesnkowe, is born in Dakhgird. The Nizdvig and the Yoheche of Dakhgird now share kin as well as streets. Runmlidy is of Human and Halfling blood.
The new rulers of Qasr Fab sweep away wage labour and decree company towns.
Over 102 years the speech of Chonini has drifted from the Yoheche tongue; its people now call themselves the Seylalkom.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Sa'lektun close the air-lanes above Tefahu, starving Vohi of the high trade.
Sailors recount dire tales of Dagon the Abyssal the Leviathan: wreckage and broken hulls wash ashore following a savage pelagic ambush.
Regency established: with young monarch Vakiveme at age 7, Lord Regent Jikdökha assumes the seal of state for Hepopo.
Bloodline awakened: Titoku of Jukobochipo manifests the hereditary Dragon-Heart curse across Mibo.
Pretender war: Grefrilla, backed by a disinherited royal uncle, contests the crown of Flipri and rallies rebel banners!
Catastrophic shaft collapse: tectonic tremors bury the great shaft between Lusyruni and Frentum, stranding the undercity in total isolation.
Sovereign credit issued: Fugger Trans-Continental Bank extends a promissory loan of 60 gold to Frentum to finance state mobilization.

Garrison at Tahokufelita repels a cross-planet invasion pouring through the Starlit Veil!
After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Wuladi give way! Vanguard forces of Vohi storm the royal seat of Hifiwesy, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
Maple Thanks: People of Nachonaki wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Nonumoho.
After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Glakru give way! Vanguard forces of Vrelrona storm the royal seat of Blia, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
The final citadels fall, and the crown of Commune of Hifiwesy is broken forever. With treasuries emptied and borders dissolved, Fedeta Risimu flees into bitter exile as the nation fades into legend.
Envoys from Vemhog and Nachonaki exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Dakhgird and Vemvuf exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Nocho and Wemapee exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
The War of Tenipa reaches its conclusion after 2 years of bloodshed: Tenipa & Sonamọba triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
Pego of Sonamọba wins the glory sought in the War of Tenipa.
ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Victorious armies from Tenipa mandate total political reorganization in Nojajokapu! Overthrowing the vanquished elite, they inaugurate the Iron Dominion of Nojajokapu.
Chiki II of Chusuyu comes to the throne bent on the safety of the nation.
Solemn rites echo through Chusuyu following the death of Chiki the Fortunate Chusupiha (old age). Chiki is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.

THE GREAT REFORMATION: In Qasr Fab, Niqbansiza nails ninety-five theses condemning clerical indulgence! Proclaiming the Reformed Covenant of Qasr Fab, reformers split from ancient dogma. Riots break out as iconoclasts smash old idols.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Litoholeti rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Bipifọ, they establish the Commune of Litoholeti with Riwa leading the commune.
Riwa is acclaimed ruler of Commune of Litoholeti.
Outraged by treason, the crown of Syndicate of Bipifọ mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Commune of Litoholeti. The War of Bipifọ begins in fire and iron.

MERCANTILE SECESSION: Wealthy patricians and merchant cartels in Witañumarca rebel against royal tariffs! Declaring commercial independence from Chusuyu, Chachiñuha establishes the Free Trading Cities of Sañilisuyu.
Chachiñuha is acclaimed ruler of Free Trading Cities of Sañilisuyu.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Commercial Union of Chusuyu dispatches punitive legions to subdue Free Trading Cities of Sañilisuyu. The bitter Chusuyu–Sañilisuyu War is underway.
A golden age of invention dawns in Sonamọba: patents multiply and the great exhibition draws the world.
Bustling market stalls and foreign merchants pack Pochowu's squares, bartering goods under Grand Imperial Subterranean Bastions & Megaliths.
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Gimi strike at midnight in Daci! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Cybernetic Union of Daci!

STATE ATHEISM PROCLAIMED: The revolutionary leadership in Daci enacts Radical Secularization! State religion is abolished, temple estates and monastery vaults are confiscated for the people (+65 gold), and ancient dogma is suppressed.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Clandestine agents from Shesnochnön sow suspicion in the frontier councils of Dudasekota.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Clandestine agents from Miheton sow suspicion in the frontier councils of Bipifọ.
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Miheton are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Bipifọ!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Dilbuna embarks upon the Recovery of the Master's Astrolabe at Qasr Shuh! Dilbuna traces a famed astrolabe to a sealed observatory room in Qasr Shuh.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Tenipa pave the Mite-Niwekota Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Mite and Niwekota (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Lokhkür pave the Lokhkür-Muryle Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Lokhkür and Muryle (+trade, +stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Khorvath the Blood Lord floods the warriors of Nojajokapu with bloodthirsty slaughter! Mortal legions butcher foes with demonic savagery (+25% army power, -8 stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Zephyros the Sky-Sovereign hurls deafening thunderbolts across the frontiers of Nusachu, scattering hostile vanguards with righteous gales (+15% army power).
Liwa, an aeronaut outlaw, raids the payroll zeppelins of Tenipa and drops the coin over the slums of Yemewayu.
Crowds in Hepopo hang on the words of Fufiwange, who calls for an eight-hour day as holy writ.
Crowds in Grov hang on the words of Travho, who calls for an eight-hour day as holy writ.
Masked engineer Citana sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Lusyruni; workers whisper the name in every pub.

Masked engineer Llagra sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Frentum; workers whisper the name in every pub.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Ngetufuroa (Ngenui); tax riots in Panuwa (Chonini).

Basdemmüsh of Dölzüj secures the line, with Basdemmüsh grown to take the crown.
Delbkuf conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Iron Plains) using magic (score 10 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Nisa survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 14 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
Kvugorod completes a great fair-city on the river at Shegrad, a marvel of the Vnovmnrehmytv people.
Wampum belts record a new treaty between Wemapee and its neighbours.
In the lands Qasr Fab won by the sword, 8 districts now speak the Dimtamkid tongue and keep its customs.
The court of Cepi bans the Lacquered Guild of Yuko'iha; its masters flee across the border.
After long debate, Duribọba lays company towns to rest and adopts wage labour.
Whispers in the fields of Ile-wolu: a call to break the lords' hold gathers the company hands against company towns.
A great fungal bloom carpets the caverns of Reda around Lusyruni; spore-bread and lamp-moss for all.
LOCUSTS: A cloud of locusts darkens the sky over Tenipa; in three days the fields around Seletikota are stripped bare.
The grain silos of Tenipa cannot make good what was lost; famine stalks the villages around Seletikota.
Requisition squads of Tenipa seize seed grain at spearpoint; the barracks are full and the fields fall silent.
Mine of Chonini attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Miraculous intervention: as enemy banners besiege Womunemotu, the sacred relic 'The Sacred Talisman' flares with blinding celestial radiance, reinforcing the ramparts!
The War of Tenipa is known as the Vindication among the Yima, and as the Aggression among the Pima.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the Great Vohi War after 1 year. With frontiers redrawn, Vohi dictate terms to the vanquished.
Upon the fertile crossroads of Mukofetu, allied elders and chieftains swear a founding compact, raising the banners of the sovereign Voyager League of Mukofetu.
Interplanetary vanguard from Siny emerges through the Hollow Door! The Rift-Dominion of Zuchibov seizes Mukofetu.
Feast of New Light: People of Dakhgird wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Dakhgird.
An ancient sovereign power falls to dust: Free City of Blia is extinguished. Royal archives smolder, and Tramga Llykkin flees into obscurity.
A victor's peace is forged: after 1 year of campaign in the Hundred Days War of Blia, Vrelrona prevail, annexing contested borderlands.
Harvest Home: Granaries of Ile-wolu are opened at Ile-wolu; the whole town eats until dusk.
Envoys from Mihopah and Tafelenui exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Dakhgird and Vemkoz exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Lokhkür and Qödgibböz exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Free Commonwealth of Tiruta launches a determined invasion into Empire of Suchino, igniting the War of Tiruta.
Neither camp can break the front: envoys sign a mutual cessation of hostilities, ending the War of Bipifọ (1 year) in an uneasy truce.
Fydi of Cigawudi takes up the cause of wealth.
Mourning envelops Cigawudi: Cafa the Bold Hasici dies of a fall from a horse. The royal scepter passes to Fydi, an underage youth of 13 years, under the stewardship of high chancellors.
Zhabkuf of Vemhog takes up the cause of wealth.
The reign of Fazslida the Great Fazsdubhpurn in Vemhog concludes with their death (old age). Zhabkuf takes up the royal mantle, vowing to defend the nation.
Yopo II of Fulomu turns from the old cause toward the safety of the nation.
The death of Ure Noneniwo (old age) leaves Fulomu without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Wilinipepuso seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.
Mukewe of Miheton turns from the old cause toward vengeance.
The bells of Miheton toll for the passing of Wawe Lionheart Wopu (poison). The youth Mukewe ascends the throne under a regency council.
MERCANTILE SECESSION: Wealthy patricians and merchant cartels in Mufufofe rebel against royal tariffs! Declaring commercial independence from Fulomu, Yone establishes the Merchant League of Netefọba.
Yone is acclaimed ruler of Merchant League of Netefọba.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Republic of Fulomu dispatches punitive legions to subdue Merchant League of Netefọba. The bitter Netefọba Campaign is underway.
Derepome (Master Artificer) designs a rapid-firing ballista mechanism adopted by frontier garrisons in Tosesemolowe.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Kil-hycame divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Ganiwowa!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Hepopo are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Sañilisuyu!

The Cruvrenre Campaign is known as the Rightful War in Vliclu, and as the Unprovoked War in Cruvrenre.
Over the centuries Sowegodan has worn down on the tongue into Sowegdan; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Chonini has worn down on the tongue into Choneni; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Wovoru has worn down on the tongue into Wovor; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Night of Shadow Plays: Scholars and singers of Kegonani compete in Hokewati; the best verse is carried through the streets.
Feast of Breaking the Fast: Bonfires on the hills of Zufqan greet the high sun above Zufqan.
Feast of the Return Voyage: Boats of Puwiwa are blessed and raced off Puwiwa; sailors are toasted ashore.
Rice Blessing: Granaries of Hokewati are opened at Hokewati; the whole town eats until dusk.
Green Corn Feast: Granaries of Yunuwagi are opened at Yunuwagi; the whole town eats until dusk.
Envoys from Ngenui and Lokhkür exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
A public scaffold execution in Pochowu's plaza draws murmuring crowds beneath the High Citadel Throne Monument; royal decree enforces order.
Master Artificer Daqa of Khihozibo achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "The Compound Lever Crane".
Wi'kasa (Grand Champion) defeats a formidable foreign dragoon in single combat before the royal court in Sa'lektun.
Siynaylaba (Grand Champion) sets an unprecedented record in the sprint and javelin throwing trials in Famlam.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Nomzekjima storm the government palace in Chöshjum! The faction seizes control, establishing the Grand Duchy of Chöshjum.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Niqino as a mass uprising topples the throne of Republic of Niqino! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Kha proclaims the sovereign People's Republic of Niqino!

STATE ATHEISM PROCLAIMED: The revolutionary leadership in Niqino enacts Radical Secularization! State religion is abolished, temple estates and monastery vaults are confiscated for the people (+65 gold), and ancient dogma is suppressed.
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Piñarasuyu are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Vemhog!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Vrelrona are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Wuñi!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Vlofre divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Yunuwagi!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Vlofre are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Yunuwagi!
QUEST COMPLETED: Search for the Buried Stela of Bunokab! Ko'a raises the stela and the city reads its count again, bringing the sacred relic Ancient Circlet of Nuri!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: To'luchu embarks upon the Search for the Buried Stela of Le'wu! To'luchu hears that a founding stela was buried by jungle growth near Le'wu.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Smia pave the Tluspo-Cigawudi Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Tluspo and Cigawudi (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Vemhog pave the Veftpush-Khonnabad Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Veftpush and Khonnabad (+trade, +stability).
The Mite–Halithani Railway of Tenipa reaches Meligihetopa: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Nyxal the Void Dreamer projects psychic void-whispers into the foes of Mibo! Invaders flee in weeping delirium, haunted by visions of tentacled cosmic voids (+18% army power, -7 stability).

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Gilọ rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Polego, they establish the People's Republic of Gilọ with Ega leading the commune.
Ega is acclaimed ruler of People's Republic of Gilọ.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Merchant League of Polego dispatches punitive legions to subdue People's Republic of Gilọ. The bitter Great Polego War is underway.
Masked engineer Keningu sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Suhonunanga; workers whisper the name in every pub.
Bread riots seize Polego! Mill-hands and dockers storm the steam bakeries, smashing gauges and demanding cheaper loaves from Polego.

Nomzekjima of Chöshjum comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.

Mildarqaf conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Iron Plains) using tactic (score 13 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Vribra survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 12 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
Nations of Ganiwowa gather at Ganiwowa for a great council and dances that last through the night.
Astronomers of Le'wu predict the eclipse to the day; Ix-cha celebrates the turning of a great cycle.
The Hollow Players of Grov finds patrons in Qasr Fab.
Laybas ibn Susdafhib al-Qalshiswad founds the Sober Brotherhood in Zandim; its pamphlets call for temperance across Qasr Fab.
The new rulers of Niqino sweep away wage labour and decree workers' cooperatives.
A cave-in thunders through Shegrad; Kvugorod digs for survivors for weeks.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Flicrona bars the shaft to Cigari, and the tithe-collectors of Daci are turned back at the lamps of Biqnockhot.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Zufqan close the air-lanes above Qasr Fab, starving Qasr Fab of the high trade.
A whirlwind walks across the plains of Litoholeti in late spring and through the heart of Daha, scattering roofs like leaves.
Yoro of Wewọ attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Bloodline awakened: Rildyimba of Tibshed manifests the hereditary Giant Stature curse across Babfazh.
TITAN REAWAKENING: After centuries of primordial slumber, the immortal The Emerald Qilin (Emerald Qilin) awakens in Wilds beyond Tehu! Its primeval fury shakes the continent.

monsters.name: The Deep Lake Wyrm
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: Lion of the Golden Dawn
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Celestial Raptor
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: The Great Calydonian Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: Titan of the Steppes
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: The Rime-Bane
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: Roc the Sky-Render
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: The Forest Sasabonsam
monsters.lore: A long-legged forest being that dangles from the canopy to snatch the careless traveller.

monsters.name: The Ifrit of the Brass Bottle
monsters.lore: A spirit of smokeless fire, proud and cunning, bound by old seals and older bargains.

monsters.name: Timingila the Whale-Swallower
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

monsters.name: The All-Knowing Simurgh
monsters.lore: A vast and wise bird that has seen the world destroyed three times; it may help a hero or test them.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards
