prayers: Zirhiw, first of the high seats, and the Bright Child, hear us together.
Many gods, one town: Zirhiw, bless Zirdab, and the others bless what Zirhiw forgets.
The Bright Child for the fields, the Ferryman for the roads, Zirhiw for all that remains.
Zirhiw, lord of the high seat, let the Ferryman guard my journey and the Bright Child my sleep.
Let the oak outlive me and the acorn outlive the oak.
Root and leaf of Zirdab, Zirhiw walks among you; I will not cut without asking.

liturgy.name: The Seed Service
steps: The faithful gather beneath the oldest tree and bare their heads.
A branch is struck softly, and the answer listened for in the leaves.
Each faithful lays a seed or a handful of water at the roots.
A verse is spoken from memory; the printed psalter stays closed in a grove.
The archdruid walks the circle blessing each tree by name.
A fallen branch is gathered, never cut, to feed the fire.
The faithful leave a plain gift of loaf at the trunk and go quietly.

scripture.title: The Book of the Open Hand
excerpts: Verse: A bird’s quarrel is wiser than a king’s decree.
Law: For every tree felled, plant two, and tell the grove.
Parable of the Three Gifts: Each god gave a man a gift, and he kept the one he used least.
Verse: The forest does not hurry, and is never late.
Law: When you pass a shrine, leave a coin or a kind word, to whichever god is nearest.
Verse: The oak is the elder of the world; bend your head.
Law: Never swear by a god you have not fed.
Verse: Zirhiw may rule the high seat, but the Bright Child holds the keys to the larder.
Parable of the Axeman: He cut the old ash and the spring went dry beneath it.

holyDays.name: Midsummer Rest

holyDays.name: Feast of First Fruit

Lalqefmukh, who wore the first crown, advise the ones who wear it now.
Lalqefmukh, let my hands be a bowl for the hungry and a roof for the cold.
Make me gentle to the beast and the beggar, Lalqefmukh, even when they are not gentle to me.

The faithful leave in pairs and carry what is left to the doors of the sick.

prayers: Between Sacmeg and the Devourer the world is stretched: let me not be torn.
The Devourer is patient; Sacmeg, be more patient still.
Sacmeg, in the long war, count me a soldier, not a prize.
Sacmeg, light of the first morning, hold back the Devourer from this house tonight.
Stone above stone, Sacmeg, let me set one more and not be crushed.
We build what we cannot understand; Sacmeg, hold the keystone.

liturgy.name: The Setting of the Stone
steps: The faithful assemble at a half-built wall in the chapel court.
The abyssal hierophant lays a cord along the ground and calls the angle true or false.
Each faithful carries a stone from the quarry and sets it in order.
The creed is chanted in a rhythm to match the setting of each block.
The keystone is touched, the steam whistle struck once.
The abyssal hierophant walks the wall’s edge reading the number of the course.
No mortar is used on the holy course, only weight and patience.
The faithful depart facing the wall, backing out until the gate.

scripture.title: The Roll of the Quiet Hour
excerpts: Law: In every choice, ask which power it feeds.
Law: Raise the wall in even courses, and do not ask what it keeps out.
Parable of the Crooked Angle: A mason bent a corner and the whole hall learned to lean.
Law: No light shall touch the lowest stone.
Law: The measure of the holy is the number of its courses, not its beauty.
Verse: Two hands made the world: one lit it, one was jealous.
Parable of the Two Doors: A traveller took the door that looked brighter, and found the dark behind it.
Verse: The long war is fought one small kindness at a time.
Verse: The stone remembers what the mason forgets.

saints.name: Saint Awa the Redeemed Martyr
saints.legend: Awa walked unarmed to the enemy camp and was killed; the army broke camp the next morning. Canonised in year 170.

saints.name: Saint Ara the Comforter of the Weak
saints.legend: Ara gave a cloak to a beggar who was later found to be Sacmeg in disguise. Canonised in year 130.

saints.name: Saint Ike the Comforter of the Weak
saints.legend: Ike gave a cloak to a beggar who was later found to be Sacmeg in disguise. Canonised in year 90.

heresies.name: Koteite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the true line of teaching was broken by the abyssal hierophant of the mother faith.

heresies.name: The Soft Builders
heresies.claim: Holds that the wall is a prison and not a shrine.

heresies.name: The Crooked Course
heresies.claim: Holds that Sacmeg cares nothing for stone.

heresies.name: The Unmeasured
heresies.claim: Holds that mortar and craft are no sin.

lore.afterlife: The soul is claimed by light or dark; most are claimed by both and must be sorted by the long war.

holyDays.name: Night of the Lowest Chamber
holyDays.rite: A single gas lamp is carried to the deepest room and left there.

holyDays.name: The Setting of the Stone
holyDays.rite: A new block is laid in the great wall and measured by the abyssal hierophant.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Keystone
holyDays.rite: The faithful gather beneath the keystone and sing the low note.

blessings: May your gas lamp burn through the night.
sins: entering the lowest chamber with a light
setting a stone out of order
swearing falsely in the name of Sacmeg
defiling the chapel with a brawl

clergy.greetStranger: Do not touch the walls.
clergy.title: Abyssal Hierophant

observances: Never speak above a murmur in the chapel.
Measure your own house by the holy angles.
Bring one stone each year to the great wall.
Settle your quarrels before the holy day.

prayers: I do not curse the Shadow Under; I only ask Nganabo to arrive first.
The Shadow Under is patient; Nganabo, be more patient still.
Nganabo, in the long war, count me a soldier, not a prize.
Let my left hand do the shadow’s work no more; let my right keep the gas lamp of Nganabo.
Nganabo, steady the shield arm and sharpen the vow; we do not march alone.
Let me be the wall at Katala, Nganabo, and let the wall hold.

liturgy.name: The Vigil of Arms
steps: The faithful gather armed at the chapel door and ground their weapons.
The grand inquisitor walks the ranks and checks each oath.
The creed is chanted in the cadence of a march.
Blades are raised to Nganabo and returned unblooded.
The grand inquisitor names the enemy of the season and the ground to hold.
Bread and sour wine are taken standing.
The steam whistle sounds three times; the ranks file out as they came.

scripture.title: The Wisdom of the Water and the Stone
excerpts: Verse: We do not hate the heathen; we are sent past them.
Law: You shall not lie to the light, nor flatter the dark.
Verse: Peace is the reward of those who held the line.
Law: A faithful soldier owes the grand inquisitor one obedience and no more.
Law: The sword is drawn only for the faith, and sheathed only for the dead.
Parable of the Wall: One stone fell and a city followed.
Law: In every choice, ask which power it feeds.
Verse: the Shadow Under does not hate you. It only waits.
Verse: Two hands made the world: one lit it, one was jealous.

saints.name: Saint Ala the White Lily
saints.legend: Ala kept a single gas lamp alive in Nufigo for a lifetime without letting it gutter. Canonised in year 110.

saints.name: Workospag the Mender
saints.legend: Workospag first wrote down the sayings and burned the draft that was too proud.

heresies.name: Netegaite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the true line of teaching was broken by the grand inquisitor of the mother faith.

heresies.name: The Gentle Shield
heresies.claim: Holds that the enemy of the faith is within, not beyond.

heresies.name: The Weepers at the Gate
heresies.claim: Holds that the holy sword is a shame and the shield alone is holy.

heresies.name: The Peacemakers of the Line
heresies.claim: Holds that martial vows are a snare of the grand inquisitor.

lore.afterlife: After death the soul stands on a narrow bridge; what it carried decides which way it leans.

holyDays.name: The Blessing of Banners
holyDays.rite: The grand inquisitor sprinkles every standard with wine and ash.

holyDays.name: The Vigil of Arms
holyDays.rite: A night spent awake with the weapon laid before the altar.

holyDays.name: The Victory March
holyDays.rite: The host parades past the chapel to the beat of a single drum.

blessings: May your oath be heavier than your blade.
May the faithful stand at your back.
sins: sparing a sworn enemy of the faith
breaking a vow sworn at the chapel
swearing falsely in the name of Nganabo

clergy.greetFaithful: At ease, {name}. The line holds because of you.
clergy.greetStranger: Unbeliever or friend? Say it plain.
clergy.title: Grand Inquisitor

observances: Never lay your arms among unbelievers.
Answer the muster bell at once.
Drill with the faithful each week.
Say a short prayer before every meal.

prayers: Ko'uki, who needs no second, be the first thing I name and the last.
Ko'uki, you alone made the hills and Kabawu; hear a small voice.
There is no god but Ko'uki; to Ko'uki I give the morning and the gas lamp.
Ko'uki, one and only, keep this house under your single eye.
Grant that I be born again to the rank I earn by doing this one well.
Let each keep the post Ko'uki set, the hand to the plough and the mind to the book.

liturgy.name: The Seating of the Ranks
steps: The faithful enter by the door of their station, the high first and the low last.
The high brahmin lights the gas lamp and names the duty of each rank aloud.
Each rank answers with its own line of the creed.
The printed psalter is read from the page of the day.
Each house brings its tithe in the goods of its trade.
The high brahmin blesses the tithe, and the lowest rank is fed first, as the rule requires.
The vows of station are renewed together.
The ranks leave in reverse, and no one speaks across a boundary until the door is passed.

scripture.title: The Book of the Long Road
excerpts: Law: Marry within your station; the line is the first obligation.
Law: The seventh day is Ko'uki’s; let the ox and the servant rest with you.
In the beginning Ko'uki spoke once, and the speaking is the world.
Verse: The river does not argue with its banks.
Law: The high shall not strike the low; the low shall not speak first to the high.
Law: You shall bear no second name before Ko'uki, neither in jest nor in need.
Parable of the Lamp: A man hid his gas lamp under a bowl, and walked into a well.
Law: The hand belongs to its work; the work belongs to its house.
Verse: A rank is not a cage but a bridge for the one who walks it with grace.

saints.name: Saint Nifkhoma the Comforter of the Weak
saints.legend: Nifkhoma fed a besieged town from a single pot and was found dead of hunger, the pot still warm. Canonised in year 140.

saints.name: Po'ne of the Long Road
saints.legend: Po'ne judged a feud between brothers and left both of them in tears of shame.

heresies.name: Yetaite Heresy
heresies.claim: Holds that the true line of teaching was broken by the high brahmin of the mother faith.

heresies.name: The Levellers of the Quarter
heresies.claim: Holds that marriage across ranks is blessed by Ko'uki.

heresies.name: The Crossed Hands
heresies.claim: Holds that the tithe of the low is worth more than the high’s.

lore.afterlife: At death Ko'uki weighs each life once; the light are lifted and the heavy are left to be lightened.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Four Tools
holyDays.rite: Plough, pen, sword and scales are blessed on the chapel steps.

holyDays.name: The Walk of the Gate
holyDays.rite: All ranks walk the boundary of the quarter and mend what is broken.

holyDays.name: The Weighing of Tithes
holyDays.rite: Houses bring the year’s goods and the lowest rank is fed first.

holyDays.name: Night of the Returning
holyDays.rite: The faithful recite the names of past lives, one rank at a time.

blessings: May the rank bless you as you bless it.
sins: taking up a trade not your own
speaking first to a higher rank
defiling the chapel with a brawl
breaking a vow sworn at the chapel

clergy.greetFaithful: Hail, {name}. Keep your station and be at peace.
clergy.greetStranger: Traveller, state your house and rank, and I will know how to greet you.
clergy.title: High Brahmin

observances: Teach your craft to your own line only.
Never eat with a lower rank.
Renew station vows each new year.
Give a tithe to the chapel each season.

prayers: I set out loaf and the gas lamp for those who walked here before.
We are the leaves, Nakaju is the root; let the root drink well.
Blood of Nakaju, blood in me; let me not shame the name.
Fathers and mothers behind me, Nakaju at the head: stand at my back.
Let the pass hold and the vein run; Nakaju, we pay you in labour and in silence.
Old stone, Nakaju in the deep: I keep the oath my fathers swore with you.

liturgy.name: The Descent Service
steps: The faithful carry lamps down to the lowest chamber of the chapel.
The runepriest lays a palm on the living rock and listens.
The old pact is read aloud in the oldest words, no changes allowed.
Each house presents a tool of its craft to be touched to the stone.
The steam whistle is struck on stone and the echo timed.
A new oath is cut on the wall by a mason, a letter at a time.
The faithful climb out in order of age, eldest last.

scripture.title: The Teaching of the Long Road
excerpts: Verse: Under the root is the root of the world.
Verse: A house without a grave has not been lived in.
Law: The eldest speaks first and the youngest keeps the lamp.
Verse: Stone is the oldest oath; do not break what is older than you.
Law: The mountain gives, the mountain keeps. Take no more than the pact allows.
Verse: We are the ones who were told to carry on.
Parable of the Forgotten Name: A line forgot its grandfather, and its fields would not bear.
Law: A debt to the mountain is paid in labour and in silence.
Verse: Where the echo is longest, the pact is oldest.

saints.name: Numdisa the Unbroken
saints.legend: Numdisa stood alone against a raiding band and turned them with a single word.

saints.name: Dunjifdis the Unbroken
saints.legend: Dunjifdis judged a feud between brothers and left both of them in tears of shame.

saints.name: Jufdissisa the Lamp-bearer
saints.legend: Jufdissisa sheltered a village in a harsh winter and was never seen again after the thaw.

heresies.name: The Surface Folk
heresies.claim: Holds that the echo is only air.

heresies.name: The Deep Doubters
heresies.claim: Holds that the holy seam may be cut for the common good.

heresies.name: The Open Miners
heresies.claim: Holds that Nakaju lives in the open and not the deep.

lore.afterlife: The dead join the line behind the living, watching, advising, and sometimes quarrelling.

holyDays.name: The Renewal of the Pact
holyDays.rite: The pact is read in the lowest chamber and sealed with ore.

holyDays.name: Day of Stone Offerings
holyDays.rite: Each house lays a worked stone at the mountain’s foot.

holyDays.name: Descent of Lamps
holyDays.rite: The faithful carry lit gas lamps into the deep and sing.

holyDays.name: The Day of Echoes
holyDays.rite: A great stone is struck and the length of its answer is read as an omen.

blessings: May the road be kind to your feet.
May your table never be bare.
sins: mocking the runepriest to their face
swearing falsely in the name of Nakaju

clergy.greetStranger: Surface-dweller, mind the pact.
clergy.title: Runepriest

observances: Descend to the stone hall each season.
Speak softly underground.
Pay the mountain its share of every find.
Attend the chapel on every holy day.

prayers: The world breathes, and I am one breath of it; Ponlomyi, let me breathe well.
In the gas lamp and the rain alike I see Ponlomyi; let me not be blind to either.
Ponlomyi, whole and woven, I am a thread of you; keep me from fraying.
Ponlomyi, who is the road, the walker and the dust, let me know I am not apart.
Root and leaf of Wupemsam, Ponlomyi walks among you; I will not cut without asking.
I plant before I take. Ponlomyi, remember it when you count.

liturgy.name: The Walk of the Oaks
steps: The faithful gather beneath the oldest tree and bare their heads.
The archdruid asks the trees’ leave to hold the meeting.
A branch is struck softly, and the answer listened for in the leaves.
The archdruid walks the circle blessing each tree by name.
A fallen branch is gathered, never cut, to feed the fire.
The faithful leave a plain gift of loaf at the trunk and go quietly.

scripture.title: The Sayings of the First Light
excerpts: Verse: The first prayer is attention.
Law: Take only what has fallen, and thank it for falling.
Law: No fire is lit in the grove save the holy one.
Law: To harm the least living thing is to wound the whole.
Parable of the Axeman: He cut the old ash and the spring went dry beneath it.
Verse: A bird’s quarrel is wiser than a king’s decree.
Parable of the Weaver: A weaver cut a thread and the whole cloth in Wupemsam frayed by autumn.
Verse: The forest does not hurry, and is never late.
Verse: Do not look for Ponlomyi in a temple; you are standing in one.

saints.name: Memba of the Long Road
saints.legend: Memba walked into a burning chapel and returned with the printed psalter and no scorch.

saints.name: Gemumbe the Plain Speaker
saints.legend: Gemumbe sheltered a village in a harsh winter and was never seen again after the thaw.

saints.name: Kebinbe the Gentle
saints.legend: Kebinbe first wrote down the sayings and burned the draft that was too proud.

saints.name: Wenmum the Gentle
saints.legend: Wenmum was seized by a tyrant and refused to renounce Ponlomyi to the last breath.

heresies.name: The Clear-Fellers
heresies.claim: Holds that fire is sacred anywhere.

heresies.name: The Axe Brethren
heresies.claim: Holds that Ponlomyi lives in the sky, not the trees.

heresies.name: The Open Sky
heresies.claim: Holds that the forest exists to be used.

heresies.name: The Stone Gatherers
heresies.claim: Holds that the grove is a heap of wood and nothing more.

lore.afterlife: The dead are not elsewhere, only more widely spread.

holyDays.name: Night of the Holy Fire
holyDays.rite: The only fire in the grove is lit from the oldest oak.

holyDays.name: The Planting Day
holyDays.rite: The faithful plant a sapling for each child born in the year.

holyDays.name: Midsummer Rest
holyDays.rite: No axe is lifted and no ground is broken for three days.

holyDays.name: Feast of First Fruit
holyDays.rite: The first fruit of each tree is left at the trunk.

sins: defiling the chapel with a brawl
mocking the archdruid to their face

clergy.greetStranger: You are a guest of the trees.
clergy.title: Archdruid

observances: Plant a seed every spring.
Walk the grove on each holy day.
Thank a tree each morning.
Keep the weekly rest day and give no work to others.

prayers: Old ones of the stream and the stone, Metaniki among you, forgive our feet.
Hear me, owners of the trees; the axe is hungry but I am sorry.
Metaniki, keeper of the wild things, count me among your guests and not your prey.
Metaniki, spirit of the long water, carry the day gently past my door.
I bow to the line before me, Metaniki, and promise to be bowed to by the line after.
Let the names be said and the graves be swept, and the hearth be fed.

liturgy.name: The Sweeping of the Graves
steps: The household sweeps the family shrine and lays out loaf and the gas lamp.
The eldest speaks the names of the line, back as far as they are known.
After each name, the household answers: we remember.
The patriarch asks the dead for advice on the matter of the day.
A silence is kept long enough for an answer to come, or not.
The gas lamp is left burning till it dies of its own accord.

scripture.title: The Sayings of the Salt and the Seed
excerpts: Verse: The wise ask the dead, and the foolish merely outlive them.
Law: Elders are heard before they speak.
Verse: Your father’s face is in your child’s, and both are watching you.
Law: No house shall be sold without telling its dead.
Parable of the Hunter and the Hare: A hunter killed without thanks and found no meat the next year.
Verse: The wolf prays too; listen when he sings.
Law: Sweep the graves in the season of the dead, and do not hurry.
Verse: The river is a long body; do not foul its mouth.
Verse: Every stone was somebody once; walk as if it still minds.

saints.name: Saint Ifa the Redeemed Martyr
saints.legend: Ifa refused to recant before the magistrate and was given to the crowd at Ponogofi. Canonised in year 20.

saints.name: Genupo the Lamp-bearer
saints.legend: Genupo first wrote down the sayings and burned the draft that was too proud.

heresies.name: The Unremembered
heresies.claim: Holds that one may choose one’s own line.

heresies.name: The Graveless
heresies.claim: Holds that Metaniki is a story and the dead are only gone.

lore.afterlife: A soul walks the land as a spirit for seven winters, then joins the wider wild.

holyDays.name: Night of the Hearth
holyDays.rite: Every household keeps its hearth lit through the dark and calls the dead.

holyDays.name: Sweeping of the Graves
holyDays.rite: Families clean and feed the graves of the line.

holyDays.name: The Naming of the Newborn
holyDays.rite: Children born in the year are named after the dead of the line.

holyDays.name: Day of the Return
holyDays.rite: Those living far away come home to eat at the family table.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Names
holyDays.rite: The eldest recites the whole line before the shared meal.

blessings: May your name be spoken after.
sins: forgetting the names of the line

clergy.greetStranger: Welcome to our hearth. Mind the elders.
clergy.title: Patriarch

observances: Sweep the shrine each week.
Keep the hearth fed.
Speak the names of the line at the evening meal.
Settle your quarrels before the holy day.

prayers: Many gods, one town: Hutalitu, bless Siwuqañawuqa, and the others bless what Hutalitu forgets.
Hutalitu, first of the high seats, and the Bright Child, hear us together.
The Bright Child, turn your face to us; Hutalitu, keep your thunder in its sack.
We light a gas lamp to each of you: Hutalitu, the Bright Child, the Forge-Elder. Do not quarrel over the smoke.
Hutalitu, grant me a free tongue and a free road, and the courage to use both.
Let no lord stand between me and Hutalitu, nor any priest who takes his coin.

liturgy.name: The Open Circle
steps: All gather in a ring, with no seat higher than another.
The elder guide sits among them and speaks last, never first.
Any person may name a chain they wish struck off.
The gas lamp is passed from hand to hand around the circle.
A short verse on the freedom of Hutalitu is read by whoever holds the gas lamp.
A knotted cord is cut for each chain named.
Debts and grudges are spoken and forgiven where possible.
The ring breaks and no one is told when to leave.

scripture.title: The Ledger of Seven Winters
excerpts: Law: A debt that grows beyond its loan is theft, and may be refused.
Verse: Hutalitu may rule the high seat, but the Bright Child holds the keys to the larder.
Verse: The gods made the world in a quarrel and finished it in a feast.
Law: None shall be held who does not wish to be held.
Verse: A lord’s seat is made of the backs of those who knelt.
Law: Never swear by a god you have not fed.
Law: Priest and ploughman answer to Hutalitu in the same voice.
Parable of the Open Door: A prisoner stayed in his cell for love of the keeper, and was freed by his own hand.
Parable of the Three Gifts: Each god gave a man a gift, and he kept the one he used least.

saints.name: Qichipa who Listened
saints.legend: Qichipa walked into a burning chapel and returned with the printed psalter and no scorch.

saints.name: Ñuhuka the Gentle
saints.legend: Ñuhuka was seized by a tyrant and refused to renounce Hutalitu to the last breath.

saints.name: Quñumu of the Long Road
saints.legend: Quñumu gave away the whole of a rich inheritance and died with only a bowl.

saints.name: Yuquticha the Unbroken
saints.legend: Yuquticha judged a feud between brothers and left both of them in tears of shame.

heresies.name: The Gentle Yoke
heresies.claim: Holds that the chain is a blessing and a teacher.

heresies.name: The Kneeling Few
heresies.claim: Holds that the elder guide should rule as well as guide.

heresies.name: The Obedient
heresies.claim: Holds that freedom without order is ruin.

lore.afterlife: Heroes feast at the table of Hutalitu; the common dead drift to the quiet fields of the Bright Child.

holyDays.name: Night of Open Doors
holyDays.rite: Every house leaves its door unlatched until dawn.

holyDays.name: The Breaking of Chains
holyDays.rite: Symbolic bonds are cut in the square and debts forgiven where possible.

holyDays.name: Day Without Rank
holyDays.rite: Lord and labourer sit at the same table and swap tasks.

holyDays.name: The Open Voice
holyDays.rite: Any may speak in the square without fear of reprisal.

blessings: May the work of your hands outlast you.
May your gas lamp burn through the night.
sins: defiling the chapel with a brawl

clergy.greetFaithful: Sit, {name}. No one here sits higher.
clergy.greetStranger: You are free to stay or go, stranger.
clergy.title: Elder Guide

observances: Forgive one debt each year.
Sit in the circle without rank.
Offer the runaway a night’s shelter.
Attend the chapel on every holy day.

prayers: Fathers and mothers behind me, Noge at the head: stand at my back.
Let the dead be fed and the living honoured, Noge, in that order.
Noge, who wore the first crown, advise the ones who wear it now.
We are the leaves, Noge is the root; let the root drink well.
Noge, let my hands be a bowl for the hungry and a roof for the cold.
May no one at my door go unfed, and none at my bed go unwept.

liturgy.name: The Feeding and the Telling
steps: The chapel doors are opened and the sick and hungry are led in before the faithful.
The abbot of mercy washes the hands of the first guest.
The wounded are tended in a side room while a verse is read.
The printed psalter is read, a little, by the gas lamp.
Those with plenty lay their gifts on the alms table without being watched.
The abbot of mercy asks aloud who is without a bed tonight and finds one.
The faithful leave in pairs and carry what is left to the doors of the sick.

scripture.title: The Law of the Deep Roots
excerpts: Parable of the Bowl: A man gave his last bowl to a stranger and found it full each morning.
Verse: We are the ones who were told to carry on.
Verse: Mercy is not weakness, but a harder kind of strength.
Verse: A house without a grave has not been lived in.
Parable of the Forgotten Name: A line forgot its grandfather, and its fields would not bear.
Law: A guest is fed before they are asked their name.
Law: You shall take no life for food that can be had without it.
Verse: Noge wore the first crown so you might not have to.
Verse: Feed the one before you; the one behind you will be fed by another.

saints.name: Tetada the Plain Speaker
saints.legend: Tetada lived for years in a hollow tree and was fed by birds.

saints.name: Weta the Gentle
saints.legend: Weta gave away the whole of a rich inheritance and died with only a bowl.

saints.name: Duwa the Patient
saints.legend: Duwa walked into a burning chapel and returned with the printed psalter and no scorch.

heresies.name: The Sharp-Handed
heresies.claim: Holds that the hungry deserve their hunger.

heresies.name: The Hard Bread
heresies.claim: Holds that flesh may be eaten without sin.

lore.afterlife: The dead join the line behind the living, watching, advising, and sometimes quarrelling.

holyDays.name: Night of the Lamps for the Lost
holyDays.rite: A gas lamp is set at the door for each missing soul.

holyDays.name: Feast of the Common Pot
holyDays.rite: All households bring one dish to a shared table in the square.

holyDays.name: Day of Gentle Hands
holyDays.rite: No animal is slaughtered; the faithful eat only what the earth gives.

holyDays.name: The Healing Walk
holyDays.rite: The abbot of mercy walks the streets and blesses every invalid door.

blessings: May you be fed as you feed.
May you be healed as you heal.
May the work of your hands outlast you.
May your gas lamp burn through the night.
sins: eating while another starves at your door

clergy.greetStranger: Come in from the road, stranger. There is a bowl and a bed.
clergy.title: Abbot of Mercy

observances: Forgive one wrong each month.
Eat no flesh on holy days.
Give away a tenth of what you have.
Light a gas lamp and name Noge at the start of each day.

prayers: Gods of the many hands, Mahtloh, the Ferryman and the Forge-Elder, share this loaf among you.
We light a gas lamp to each of you: Mahtloh, the Ferryman, the Forge-Elder. Do not quarrel over the smoke.
Mahtloh, first of the high seats, and the Ferryman, hear us together.
The Ferryman for the fields, the Forge-Elder for the roads, Mahtloh for all that remains.
Make me gentle to the beast and the beggar, Mahtloh, even when they are not gentle to me.
Mahtloh, let my hands be a bowl for the hungry and a roof for the cold.

liturgy.name: The Feeding and the Telling
steps: The chapel doors are opened and the sick and hungry are led in before the faithful.
The abbot of mercy washes the hands of the first guest.
A common pot is served to all, beggar and elder alike.
The wounded are tended in a side room while a verse is read.
The printed psalter is read, a little, by the gas lamp.
Those with plenty lay their gifts on the alms table without being watched.
The abbot of mercy asks aloud who is without a bed tonight and finds one.
The faithful leave in pairs and carry what is left to the doors of the sick.

scripture.title: The Ledger of the Deep Roots
excerpts: Law: The sick are the first in the chapel, and the last to leave.
Law: A guest is fed before they are asked their name.
Law: You shall take no life for food that can be had without it.

Law: When you pass a shrine, leave a coin or a kind word, to whichever god is nearest.
Parable of the Slighted God: A farmer forgot the Forge-Elder, and his well ran bitter for a season.
Law: Never swear by a god you have not fed.
Verse: The wound you ease is the wound you carry.
Verse: Mercy is not weakness, but a harder kind of strength.

heresies.name: The Strict Mercy

heresies.name: The Hard Bread
heresies.claim: Holds that the beggar must work for the bowl.

heresies.name: The Tough Charity
heresies.claim: Holds that mercy to the wicked is cruelty to the good.

heresies.name: The Sharp-Handed
heresies.claim: Holds that flesh may be eaten without sin.

lore.afterlife: Heroes feast at the table of Mahtloh; the common dead drift to the quiet fields of the Ferryman.

holyDays.name: The Hospice Days
holyDays.rite: The faithful tend the sick in the chapel for three days without pay.

holyDays.name: Day of Gentle Hands
holyDays.rite: No animal is slaughtered; the faithful eat only what the earth gives.

holyDays.name: The Healing Walk
holyDays.rite: The abbot of mercy walks the streets and blesses every invalid door.

blessings: May no one go cold at your door.
May you be healed as you heal.
May you be fed as you feed.
May your table never be bare.
sins: striking a child or an animal

clergy.greetStranger: Come in from the road, stranger. There is a bowl and a bed.
clergy.title: Abbot of Mercy

observances: Eat no flesh on holy days.
Forgive one wrong each month.
Feed one hungry person each day.
Keep the weekly rest day and give no work to others.

prayers: All things are Aqxoyz thinking; may my small thought be a kind one.
May A'zetxokk and I be one mind a little longer, Aqxoyz.
Aqxoyz, whole and woven, I am a thread of you; keep me from fraying.
Aqxoyz, who is the road, the walker and the dust, let me know I am not apart.
Let the pass hold and the vein run; Aqxoyz, we pay you in labour and in silence.
Under the peak the pact stands. Let it outlast me.

steps: The faithful carry lamps down to the lowest chamber of the chapel.
The runepriest lays a palm on the living rock and listens.
Ore or gem from the new cutting is laid on the altar for the mountain’s share.
A new oath is cut on the wall by a mason, a letter at a time.
The faithful climb out in order of age, eldest last.

scripture.title: The Book of Many Doors
excerpts: Verse: Stone is the oldest oath; do not break what is older than you.
Parable of the Greedy Delver: He cut past the mark and the roof forgot him.
Verse: The first prayer is attention.
Parable of the Weaver: A weaver cut a thread and the whole cloth in A'zetxokk frayed by autumn.
Law: Use, and return. Take, and replant.
Law: A debt to the mountain is paid in labour and in silence.
Law: The mountain gives, the mountain keeps. Take no more than the pact allows.
Verse: The sea does not own the wave; neither do you own your thoughts.
Verse: Under the root is the root of the world.

saints.name: Saint Ehqeghtoxy the White Lily
saints.legend: Ehqeghtoxy walked away from a crown and was found a week later tending goats. Canonised in year 10.

saints.name: Ghuxtah the Plain Speaker

prayers: The Keeper of Roads for the fields, the Salt Mother for the roads, Kopsup for all that remains.
Many gods, one town: Kopsup, bless Kijwuch, and the others bless what Kopsup forgets.
Kopsup, lord of the high seat, let the Salt Mother guard my journey and the Keeper of Roads my sleep.
The Keeper of Roads, turn your face to us; Kopsup, keep your thunder in its sack.
Let the oak outlive me and the acorn outlive the oak.
I plant before I take. Kopsup, remember it when you count.

liturgy.name: The Grove Meeting
steps: The faithful gather beneath the oldest tree and bare their heads.
The archdruid asks the trees’ leave to hold the meeting.
A verse is spoken from memory; the printed psalter stays closed in a grove.
The archdruid walks the circle blessing each tree by name.
The faithful leave a plain gift of loaf at the trunk and go quietly.

scripture.title: The Book of the Deep Roots
excerpts: Law: Never swear by a god you have not fed.

Verse: The oak is the elder of the world; bend your head.
Law: For every tree felled, plant two, and tell the grove.
Verse: The forest does not hurry, and is never late.
Law: No fire is lit in the grove save the holy one.

Verse: The gods made the world in a quarrel and finished it in a feast.
Verse: Kopsup may rule the high seat, but the Keeper of Roads holds the keys to the larder.

prayers: We drink to ruin, and ask Nganabo to spare the drinker for one more night.
Nganabo, make me strong by taking from me; let me be worth the taking.
Let the rule slip and the gas lamp gutter; Nganabo, we ask for the change.
Nothing holds, nothing stays: praise to Nganabo who keeps it moving.
What is hidden is hidden for a reason: Nganabo, be that reason.
I know the first letter. Nganabo, grant me the second and the silence after.

liturgy.name: The Sealed Reading
steps: The doors are barred and the gas lamp is covered but one.
Each initiate whispers a word of the day to the one beside them.
The hierophant reads from the printed psalter in the cipher, and no one writes anything down.
A question is asked that has no answer, and is left unanswered.
The pass-sign is given hand to hand in the dark.
The gas lamp is uncovered and the first circle recites the closing line.
The hierophant burns the day’s notes, and all depart by different doors.

scripture.title: The Law of Seven Winters
excerpts: Parable of the Open Book: A fool read all of it and understood a third.
Law: Take what is offered, and what is not.
Law: What is told outside the circle is no longer true.
Law: Write nothing you could not burn.
Verse: Praise the crack in the wall; light enters.
Verse: The first truth is that there are more truths.
Law: Each initiate shall teach one, and tell no one who taught them.
Parable of the Ash King: He bound the chaos in law, and the law burned him.
Verse: The order of things is a thin ice. We are the thaw.

lore.afterlife: No judgement, only appetite; the dead feed what comes next.

holyDays.name: Night of Unspoken Names
holyDays.rite: No name is said aloud from dusk to dawn.

holyDays.name: The Burning of Notes
holyDays.rite: All written records of the year are burnt in the inner court.

holyDays.name: The Quiet Fast
holyDays.rite: Members fast and speak no word until the steam whistle sounds.

blessings: May you keep your own counsel.
May the veil lift for you.
May your gas lamp burn through the night.
sins: speaking of the closed hour outside it
swearing falsely in the name of Nganabo
mocking the hierophant to their face

clergy.greetStranger: You stand at a door. Think before you knock.
clergy.title: Hierophant

observances: Speak of the mysteries to no outsider.
Seek one new insight each season.
Keep the cipher in your head, never on paper.
Keep the weekly rest day and give no work to others.

prayers: Reformed Ko'uki, you alone made the hills and Kebime; hear a small voice.
Reformed Ko'uki, one and only, keep this house under your single eye.
Reformed Ko'uki, who needs no second, be the first thing I name and the last.
One maker, one judge: Reformed Ko'uki, weigh me gently and do not look away.
Let each keep the post Reformed Ko'uki set, the hand to the plough and the mind to the book.
I do my own work and not another’s; so the world stays whole, Reformed Ko'uki.

liturgy.name: The Ordered Hours
steps: The faithful enter by the door of their station, the high first and the low last.
The high brahmin lights the gas lamp and names the duty of each rank aloud.
The printed psalter is read from the page of the day.
Each house brings its tithe in the goods of its trade.
The high brahmin blesses the tithe, and the lowest rank is fed first, as the rule requires.
The vows of station are renewed together.
The ranks leave in reverse, and no one speaks across a boundary until the door is passed.

scripture.title: The Roll of the Long Road
excerpts: Verse: The humblest duty done well outweighs the highest done ill.
Parable of the Lamp: A man hid his gas lamp under a bowl, and walked into a well.
Law: Marry within your station; the line is the first obligation.
Law: The hand belongs to its work; the work belongs to its house.
Verse: Every hair on your head is counted, and not one wasted.
In the beginning Reformed Ko'uki spoke once, and the speaking is the world.
Verse: A rank is not a cage but a bridge for the one who walks it with grace.
Verse: What you owe Reformed Ko'uki you cannot pay, and so you are asked only to try.
Law: The high shall not strike the low; the low shall not speak first to the high.

I do my own work and not another’s; so the world stays whole, Reformed Nganabo.
Grant that I be born again to the rank I earn by doing this one well.

steps: The doors are barred and the gas lamp is covered but one.
Each initiate whispers a word of the day to the one beside them.
The first circle answers, the second listens, the third leaves.
A question is asked that has no answer, and is left unanswered.
The gas lamp is uncovered and the first circle recites the closing line.
The hierophant burns the day’s notes, and all depart by different doors.

events.text: Dinobedo Outlaw Lair raided trade routes near Dinobedo, siphoning 12 gold into their hoard.
Yasokura Outlaw Lair raided trade routes near Yasokura, siphoning 10 gold into their hoard.
Kechkas Outlaw Lair raided trade routes near Kechkas, siphoning 4 gold into their hoard.
Rubaka of Nugaga comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Marnurfola of Qitiyya comes to the throne bent on glory.
Suta of Tukacocha comes to the throne bent on the safety of the nation.
Haso of Dotedesa comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
Dinsa of Sipika lets the old grudge rest as the foe is no more.
Vecrir conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Whispering Sands) using magic (score 17 vs DC 8). Defeated Morrigan. Promoted to F-Rank!
Qiybuzduna survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 5 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
Whispers in the fields of Roderogi: a movement against the castes gathers the uncleared against clearance castes.
Something vast stirs in the lightless depths beneath Dumpemkon; the deep wardens double their watch.
Delvers of Aziyt break into a forgotten dwarven gallery beyond Ikhloth; the deep realm grows.
The tiny Rift-Colony of Wituma seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Balu.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Belọ bars the shaft to Siwufu, and the tithe-collectors of Libreqentum are turned back at the lamps of Riki.
Sailors recount dire tales of The Maw of Charybdis the Kraken: wreckage and broken hulls wash ashore following a savage pelagic ambush.
Lunewo of Webibuba attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Yirjira of Waqminar attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Balu's invasion through the Burning Wound into Siny was repulsed at Kosota.
Griots’ Epic Nights: Scholars and singers of Sadifuba compete in Wesudikura; the best verse is carried through the streets.
Flames engulf the towers of Qefbenreq! Soldiers of Liwehibhumi force the inner courtyards of Numia's capital; the royal garrison breaks, and the seat of power falls.
A catastrophic blow to Misenoki: legions of Guwegowe overrun the citadel of Henuna, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.
Garrisons of Sebana storm the ramparts of Lofodan, driving out the defenders of Nemi and hoisting their triumphant colors.
Rice Blessing: Granaries of Dalethani are opened at Makziw; the whole town eats until dusk.
Festival of the Ancestors: Families in Pebarobo set out lamps and food for their dead at Ile-gonaki.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of Guwegowe after 3 years. With frontiers redrawn, Guwegowe dictate terms to the vanquished.
Humbled, Cybernetic Union of Misenoki bends the knee and becomes a vassal of Guwegowe, paying yearly tribute.
ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Victorious armies from Guwegowe mandate total political reorganization in Misenoki! Overthrowing the vanquished elite, they inaugurate the Free Union of Misenoki.
Puwuma of Puroge comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Dynastic extinction strikes Puroge: Wowa dies heirless (old age). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Fapawe claims the vacant crown.
Dote III of Ile-tefu turns from the old cause toward vengeance.
The bells of Ile-tefu toll for the passing of Dote II the Hammer Gutimu (battle wounds). The youth Dote ascends the throne under a regency council.
Nobu'i of Balu comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Solemn rites echo through Balu following the death of Kucho the Bold Mapuchi (a wasting sickness). Nobu'i is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.
Grand Champion Abu of Liwumucho achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "Victor of the Colosseum".
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Wodosu strike at midnight in Puroge! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Stratocracy of Puroge!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Ila strike at midnight in Tabepegereti! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Theocracy of Tabepegereti!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Shufmash storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Ditshah proclaims the foundation of the Democratic Union of Shufmash!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Tosofọba as a mass uprising topples the throne of Merchant League of Tosofọba! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Doki proclaims the sovereign Confederation of Tosofọba!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Counterfeit letters planted by Ninọba rupture trust between Buyfaqmin and their ally Bilad Raqyaw!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Lomba divert 19 gold from the tax vaults of Sipika!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of UytR' pave the UytR'-Ix-wob Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between UytR' and Ix-wob (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Nugaga pave the Rerunarero-Sewananagara Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Rerunarero and Sewananagara (+trade, +stability).
The Qitiyya–Yuni Railway of Qitiyya reaches Susurari: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
PATRON MIRACLE: Thalor the All-Seeing Mind whispers lost epics and architectural secrets to the scholars of Kiqfudkid, ushering in an era of enlightened innovation (+14 stability, +20 gold).
PATRON MIRACLE: Zephyros the Sky-Sovereign hurls deafening thunderbolts across the frontiers of Liwutun, scattering hostile vanguards with righteous gales (+15% army power).
Crowds in Uhigh hang on the words of Ehtuky, who calls for an eight-hour day as holy writ.
Lerum, a soot-stained visionary, preaches in the Sumti smokestacks that the age of iron will end in fire and renewal.
Masked engineer Shimrakjiy sabotages the strike-breaking automatons of Al-buy; workers whisper the name in every pub.
The Society of the Last Cog gathers in the boiler vaults beneath Tudo, worshipping a great engine that, they swear, dreams.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Exxexy (WuñaliTawantin); tax riots in Mehtepec (Liwutun); bread riots in Qamaka.

Chroniclers now speak of the Khubnittec-Lizuwarukawi feud: for thirty years the Khubnittec and the Lizuwarukawi have answered every wrong with another.
Envoys from Roderogi and Bilad Sid exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.

Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Principality of Shuramisira launches a determined invasion into Free Trading Cities of Nushwih, igniting the War of Shuramisira.
Peace returns as invading hosts withdraw in disarray: Lomba & Balu defend their ancestral soil, concluding the Lomba Campaign (3 years).
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of the Buyfaqmin Crown after 1 year. With frontiers redrawn, Dalethani dictate terms to the vanquished.
ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Following decisive defeat in war, Dalethani imposes constitutional terms upon Buyfaqmin! The former rulers are ousted, and the Grand Marshalate of Buyfaqmin is inaugurated.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Hundred Days War of Kadetobhumi ends in mutual exhaustion after 1 year; borders return to former lines.
Uqxitkaqha of Ettugg turns from the old cause toward wealth.
In the royal halls of Ettugg, Ikhoxka the Restorer Izkot' breathes their last, succumbing to a wasting sickness. Uqxitkaqha ascends the ancestral throne amid solemn acclamation.
Iga of Koromone takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Solemn rites echo through Koromone following the death of Negi the Fair Fodotete (a hunting accident). Iga is crowned sovereign before the assembled court.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Yifar rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Qitiyya, they establish the Popular Commonwealth of Yifar with Wiqibu leading the commune.
Wiqibu is acclaimed ruler of Popular Commonwealth of Yifar.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, High Realm of Qitiyya marches swiftly upon Popular Commonwealth of Yifar. The drums of the Invasion of Yifar echo across the provinces.
Bustling market stalls and foreign merchants pack Gedopuwe's squares, bartering goods under Grand Imperial Sylvan Longhouses & Burrows.
Lutcho'a (Master Artisan) unveils a breathtaking marble colossus in the central plaza in Tanjik.
Jammich (Master Artificer) invents an ingenious optical telescope to survey distant constellations in Chupji'ha.
Abu (Grand Champion) sweeps all contenders in the Grand Tourney to ecstatic cheers from thousands in Liwumucho.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Qitiyya storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Mifisha proclaims the foundation of the Free Union of Qitiyya!
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Nabajaw! Chota seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Kingdom of Nabajaw!

COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Wiwajaw detonate powder stores in Yilebokura, gutting frontline regiments!

OVER-FARMING DUST BOWL: Decades of intensive cultivation and overgrazing exhaust the arid topsoil around the hinterlands of Podose. Violent dust storms sweep the plains, suffocating crops and forcing herders into exile.

NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Guwegowe pave the Guwegowe-Henuna Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Guwegowe and Henuna (+trade, +stability).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Shuramisira! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).

Griots’ Epic Nights: Scholars and singers of Sipika compete in Sumti; the best verse is carried through the streets.
Following fierce fighting along the fortifications, Susurari surrenders to Qitiyya; its magistrates swear fealty as Yifar's banner is hauled down.
A catastrophic blow to Zafduf: legions of Shufmash overrun the citadel of Zafduf, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.

Sisshibfua is acclaimed ruler of Democratic Union of Dar Zah.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Military Junta of Dalethani marches swiftly upon Democratic Union of Dar Zah. The drums of the Dar Zah Campaign echo across the provinces.
Lanterns and flagons herald a seasonal trade festival in Wesudikura, filling every inn and tavern to the rafters.

Geothermal eruption: superheated magma overflows the crucibles of Ridotefota; artisan holds suffer heavy damage.

Festival of the New Count: The longest night in Nasuj is spent by firelight in Nasuj, with stories and gifts.
Exhausted by protracted attrition, both sides sign an armistice concluding the Buyfaqmin Succession War (2 years). Scabbards are sheathed and the status quo ante is restored.
The Shushiyya–Zazubura Railway is cut: soldiers of Shuramisira tear up the railway track and the trains stop.

White banners flutter over the war camps. The Hundred Days War of Lomba ends in mutual exhaustion after 5 years; borders return to former lines.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of the Nirkiqbak Crown after 2 years. With frontiers redrawn, Nirkiqbak dictate terms to the vanquished.

ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Victorious armies from Nirkiqbak mandate total political reorganization in Zazubura! Overthrowing the vanquished elite, they inaugurate the Workers' Federation of Zazubura.

The whole town of Bini replasters its earthen mosque in a single joyful day.
The Hollow Consort of Koromone takes shape in Koromone: musicians who weave new modes into the old songs.
Riki squeezes the shaft-tolls of Lipumu; the miners of WuñaliTawantin mutter beneath the stone.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Qakuru bars the shaft to Boba, and the tithe-collectors of A'taykloth are turned back at the lamps of Qakuru.

Rain-soaked slopes slide into the valley of Cuftot, burying the lower village of Sebana.
Where the Yegenegu left its silt, the fields of Oyo-yebo now yield double; Roderogi remembers the flood with mixed feelings.

The banners of Dotedesa are raised over Loketo as victorious cohorts march in, ending Runonarono's dominion over the district.
Azogh overruns the defensive holdfasts of Kuli, annexing the town and its fertile environs from Balu.
The civic bell of Kuli tolls as magistrates and clan heads inaugurate the Industrial Combine of Nusajaw, establishing its seat of power.
Interplanetary vanguard from Siny emerges through the Burning Wound! The Rift-Dominion of Wituma seizes Kuli.
A catastrophic blow to Runonarono: legions of Dotedesa overrun the citadel of Runonarono, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.
An ancient sovereign power falls to dust: Free Union of Guwegowe is extinguished. Royal archives smolder, and Nutana Tubagunasugo flees into obscurity.

The final citadels fall, and the crown of Merchant League of Runonarono is broken forever. With treasuries emptied and borders dissolved, Loraha Lekunoho flees into bitter exile as the nation fades into legend.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the Border War of Runonarono after 4 years. With frontiers redrawn, Dotedesa dictate terms to the vanquished.
The Border War of Guwegowe reaches its conclusion after 3 years of bloodshed: Guwera triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
Feast of Breaking the Fast: Bonfires on the hills of Yifar greet the high sun above Yifar.
Following fierce fighting along the fortifications, Bonera surrenders to Riki; its magistrates swear fealty as Kotelo's banner is hauled down.

With swords drawn and ancient pacts invoked, Iron Dominion of Bilad Sid marches against Merchant League of Waqminar. The War of the Bilad Sid Crown begins. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Dalethani rally to Waqminar's side.
Ambition stirs in the courts of Merchant League of Kutimi, which openly claims dominion over Chiefdom of Axyett. The nation braces as the Border War of Axyett erupts.
Peace returns as invading hosts withdraw in disarray: Dotedesa & Roderogi defend their ancestral soil, concluding the Conquest of Dotedesa (4 years).
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of the Sebana Crown after 2 years. With frontiers redrawn, Sebana & Ponogofi & Nugaga dictate terms to the vanquished.
Humbled, Commune of Ninọba bends the knee and becomes a vassal of Sebana, paying yearly tribute.
ENFORCED REGIME CHANGE: Following decisive defeat in war, Sebana imposes constitutional terms upon Ninọba! The former rulers are ousted, and the Principality of Ninọba is inaugurated.
Through stubborn resolve, Sipika & Riki shatter the enemy offensive. The Invasion of Sipika ends after 1 year with the defenders holding firm.
Vomdekhgoc of Sebana takes up the cause of wealth.
The reign of Depfimmut the Elder Pocbedkhup in Sebana concludes with their death (battle wounds). Vomdekhgoc takes up the royal mantle, vowing to defend the nation.
Yuna of Nabajaw takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Dynastic extinction strikes Nabajaw: Pipa dies heirless (a fall from a horse). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House To'o claims the vacant crown.
Rubnutcec of Lomkhan takes up the cause of knowledge.
In Lomkhan, Cevcena the Elder Gemdakhius departs this life, succumbing to a hunting accident. The child Rubnutcec (age 6) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.
MERCANTILE SECESSION: Wealthy patricians and merchant cartels in Dotethani rebel against royal tariffs! Declaring commercial independence from Guwera, Ise establishes the Syndicate of Dotethani.
Ise is acclaimed ruler of Syndicate of Dotethani.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Empire of Guwera marches swiftly upon Syndicate of Dotethani. The drums of the Guwera–Dotethani War echo across the provinces.
A public scaffold execution in Napota's plaza draws murmuring crowds beneath the Town Hall Belfry; royal decree enforces order.

Blight and a failed coal-season leave UytR' hungry; the poorhouses overflow.
In the hungry year Ix'ightehy spends the treasury of UytR' on grain from abroad; few starve, and they remember who fed them.
Jammich (Master Artificer) constructs a magnificent clockwork astrolabe atop the harbor watchtower in Chupji'ha.

The Great Shuramisira War is known as the Holy Defence among the Lizuwarukawi, and as the Heretics' War among the Katala.
The Border War of Aziyt is known as the Rightful War among the Siwuqañawuqa, and as the Unprovoked War among the A'zetxokk.
The Balu Succession War is known as the Reclamation among the Kabawu, and as the Usurpation among the Nikete.
Over the centuries Qakuru has worn down on the tongue into Qaguru; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries Lotimi has worn down on the tongue into Lodimi; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
Over the centuries A'taykloth has worn down on the tongue into A'taykleth; the older name survives only in the chronicles.
The Timingila of the Deep (Timingila) prowls near the gates of Nemi! Guards scramble to defensive battlements.
Day of Rain Offerings: People of Baysuch wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Ix-bochliw.
Envoys from Lombec and Lawoland exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Envoys from Nabajaw and Oyo-yoga exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.

Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Principality of Shuramisira mobilizes its hosts against Commercial Union of Debawati. Banners unfurl for the Hundred Days War of Debawati.
Ambition stirs in the courts of High Realm of Siwufu, which openly claims dominion over Military Junta of Libreqentum. The nation braces as the Libreqentum Succession War erupts.
Aka of Bini takes up the cause of a lasting legacy.
The reign of Dowe the Wise Gonenoke in Bini concludes with their death (old age). Aka takes up the royal mantle, vowing to defend the nation.
Cenlol of Sebana comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
A perilous interregnum grips Sebana following the heirless death of Socfiqsiga (a wasting sickness). Retainers of House Dakhsip storm the assembly and usurp the crown.
Wunaha of Dotedesa takes up the cause of wealth.
A perilous interregnum grips Dotedesa following the heirless death of Luta (old age). Retainers of House Gutebuku storm the assembly and usurp the crown.

THE GREAT REFORMATION: In Rukopura, Hahe nails ninety-five theses condemning clerical indulgence! Proclaiming the Reformed Covenant of Rukopura, reformers split from ancient dogma. Riots break out as iconoclasts smash old idols.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Sukitu seize local grain silos and cast off the yoke of Dotedesa! The people inaugurate the People's Republic of Tokere under the stewardship of Wiki.
Wiki is acclaimed ruler of People's Republic of Tokere.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Theocracy of Dotedesa dispatches punitive legions to subdue People's Republic of Tokere. The bitter Great Dotedesa War is underway.
Bewita (Grand Champion) bestows glorious sporting renown upon the host realm in the international games in Pungomthani.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Yidenwem stir mutiny among garrison troops in Suhuti Beyond!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Yidenwem are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Suhuti Beyond!

QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Axtazzitza embarks upon the Bounty on the Dragon-Wyrm in The Timingila of the Deep! Axtazzitza tracks claw marks and scorched earth toward the lair of The Timingila of the Deep, preparing wards and weapons.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Kutimi pave the Kutimi-Axyett Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Kutimi and Axyett (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Riki pave the Riki-Lipumu Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Riki and Lipumu (+trade, +stability).
The Oyo-yebo–Nanesu Railway of Roderogi reaches Bapa: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
The Al-buy–Detengo Railway of Bilad Sid reaches Makziw: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
RUINOUS GIFT: Tzannik the Architect of Fate mutates the weave of fate in Puroge! Arcane mutations grant uncanny clairvoyance and secret gold, at the cost of civil panic (+30 gold, -6 stability).
ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Shubbog the Brood Mother spawns thousands of chittering dark young in the sacred groves of Webibuba, swarming forward under black skies (+20% army power, -6 stability).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Shuramisira! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Pestilax the Rot-Father touches the hosts of Siwufu with blissful pestilence! Rotting flesh feels no pain, turning armies into unyielding revenants (+12% army power, +10 resilience).
NATURE BLESSING: Sylvanor the Forest Horn awakens the ancient canopies of Tokere! Verdant thickets ensnare enemies and provide abundant woodland forage (+16 stability, +10% army power).

Insurrection flares in Pafidan! Declaring their liberties inviolable, the populace casts off the yoke of Sebana and rallies beneath the banner of Nefi, establishing the Artificer Directorate of Pafidan.
Nefi is acclaimed ruler of Artificer Directorate of Pafidan.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Cybernetic Union of Sebana dispatches punitive legions to subdue Artificer Directorate of Pafidan. The bitter Pafidan Campaign is underway.
Fetuwo, an aeronaut outlaw, raids the payroll zeppelins of Puroge and drops the coin over the slums of Gedopuwe.
Bread riots seize Pafidan! Mill-hands and dockers storm the steam bakeries, smashing gauges and demanding cheaper loaves from Sebana.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Berunakota (Guwera).

House To'o of Nabajaw and House Ronu of Poli were joined in royal marriage.
House Lipu of Lawoland and House Bishi of Yifar were joined in royal marriage.
Wunaha of Dotedesa fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.
Dinsa II of Sipika sets down the scholar's pursuits.
Hano conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Whispering Sands) using magic (score 19 vs DC 8). Defeated Morrigan. Promoted to F-Rank!
Hira survived descent to Layer 2 (Forest of Whispers), enduring 22 strain damage: Nausea, severe headaches, and limb numbness upon ascent. Whistle tier: blue.
Puroge completes an earthen great mosque at Oyo-wifo, a marvel of the Pagewe people.
The Hollow Consort of Koromone finds patrons in Riki.
Biqsfida bint Jurfdiz al-Rizsufjas founds the Friends of the Open Altar in Dakiyya; its pamphlets call for religious tolerance across Shufmash.
In Runonarono the Voice of the Guilds gathers crowds behind Dawo Dawo, demanding enfranchisement for Dotedesa.
A great fungal bloom carpets the caverns of Lomba around Oyo-nama; spore-bread and lamp-moss for all.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Qamaka bars the shaft to Ridotefota, and the tithe-collectors of Riki are turned back at the lamps of Qamaka.
Napu raises its port toll at Wanoti; the harbour-masters of Liwehibhumi protest.
FLOOD: The Yegenegu bursts its banks in spring; the low quarters of Nedolu are under water and the harvest of Roderogi rots in the fields.
Sailors recount dire tales of The Maw of Charybdis the Leviathan: wreckage and broken hulls wash ashore following a savage pelagic ambush.
Yanondim of Yidenwem attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Wuno of Ruhode attains royal majority at age 16; the regency council dissolves and the monarch claims full rule.
Bloodline awakened: Mapulimu of Wutu manifests the hereditary Giant Stature curse across Qakuru.
Geothermal eruption: superheated magma overflows the crucibles of Lakamu; artisan holds suffer heavy damage.
TITAN REAWAKENING: After centuries of primordial slumber, the immortal Behemoth the Earth-Shaker (Behemoth) awakens in Wilds beyond Soro! Its primeval fury shakes the continent.
Festival of the New Count: The longest night in Kelha is spent by firelight in Kelha, with stories and gifts.

monsters.name: Lion of the Golden Dawn
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: Drakon the Pyre-Lord
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: The Great Calydonian Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: The Storm Roc of the Badlands
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: Behemoth the Earth-Shaker
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: The Deep Lake Wyrm
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: Kraken the Fleet-Devourer
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: Ziz the Storm-Sovereign
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: The Ifrit of the Brass Bottle
monsters.lore: A spirit of smokeless fire, proud and cunning, bound by old seals and older bargains.

monsters.name: The Timingila of the Deep
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

monsters.name: The Basilisk of the Ruins
monsters.lore: A crowned serpent whose gaze turns the living to stone; only a mirror or a weasel defeats it.

monsters.name: The River Ninki Nanka
monsters.lore: A dragon of the mangrove swamps; it is said that to see it is to fall ill.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards
